IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) image # Apply histogram equalization to improve contrast cv2. equatizeHist (image) equalized _ image = # cmap='gray' is required so Matplotlib renders the plt . cmap= gray') put . titte( 'Equalized Image (Enhanced Contrast) I) put . axis(l off') tater put . show() Description : FAST NUCES - This code uses OpenCV to enhance the contrast of an image image correctly using a technique catted histogram equalization. First, it reads the image using the cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE flag. Instead of loading the image in color and converting it later, this flag tells OpenCV to toad it directly as a single-channel (black-and-white) image right from the start. Next, the cv2.equalizeHist() function is applied to the image. This function mathematically analyzes the distribution of pixel brightness values (the histogram). If an image is too dark, washed out, or tacks contrast, its pixel values are usually clumped together in a narrow range. Histogram equalization takes those clumped pixels and stretches them out across the entire available brightness spectrum (from O to 255). This process naturally darkens the darkest parts and tightens the tightest parts, revealing hidden details and significantly improving the overall global contrast of the image. Finally, the enhanced image is displayed intine using Matplotlib. Karachi Instructor: Talha Shahid 22
